claims.text: The target eutectic HEA consists of a disordered FCC matrix and nanoscale ordered B2 precipitates with coherent phase boundaries.
The initial microstructure contains a high density of dislocations from prior processing.
Aging at approximately 500–700 °C drives local chemical-order evolution and B2-domain coarsening in the target FCC/B2 alloy.
The proposed intermediate aging can evolve B2 domains without grain coarsening or impurity segregation.
An appropriate aging duration produces a peak in B2-domain size and phase-boundary energy.
Intermediate aging increases APB energy through the evolution of local chemical order in the B2 phase.
Local chemical-order evolution increases phase-boundary coherency strain in the target FCC/B2 alloy.
High APB energy and phase-boundary coherency strain impede dislocation motion.
Coarsening of ordered B2 domains increases the spacing between dislocation obstacles.
B2-domain coarsening raises the APB energy required for dislocations to cut the ordered domains.
The increased APB barrier changes deformation from cross-slip to planar slip in the FCC matrix.
Planar slip caused by the ordered-domain barrier produces the transient brittle state.
At higher temperatures, thermal activation permits dislocations to cut ordered B2 domains or bypass them by climb.
Thermally activated dislocation cutting, climb, or phase-boundary sliding restores ductility at higher temperatures.
The alloy will exhibit a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response as aging temperature increases.
Classical impurity-segregation or grain-coarsening embrittlement typically causes monotonic degradation with aging time or temperature.
The embrittlement regime is bounded at approximately 500–700 °C, where B2 coarsening is appreciable but thermal activation for domain cutting is insufficient.
Dislocation splitting width can be used to estimate APB energy, and in-situ TEM can distinguish planar from wavy dislocation configurations at phase boundaries.
Prior evidence demonstrates dislocation cutting, cross-slip suppression, or planar slip specifically within ordered B2 domains.

contradictions.description: The intervention defines the proposed brittle regime as occurring without impurity segregation, but the boundary states that the regime is excluded when impurity segregation is absent.

The main hypothesis lists phase-boundary decohesion as a route to ductility recovery, whereas the detailed mechanism and outcome instead invoke dislocation cutting, climb, or phase-boundary sliding. Decohesion is not reconciled with the claimed restoration of ductility.
